articles.title: ग्वालियर में सर्द होने लगी रातें और दिन, तीन दिन में 2.7 डिग्री लुढ़का अधिकतम तापमान, ठंडक बढ़ी - Nai Dunia

articles.full_text:
ग्वालियर में सर्द होने लगी रातें और दिन, तीन दिन में 2.7 डिग्री लुढ़का अधिकतम तापमान, ठंडक बढ़ी
मौसम में आ रही यह तब्दीली संकेत दे रही है कि दिन की गर्माहट धीरे-धीरे कम हो रही है।
Publish Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:39:00 AM (IST)Updated Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:39:26 AM (IST)
ठाटीपुर चौराहा से वाहन पर गर्म कपड़े पहन कर जातीं महिलाएं। नईदुनिया HighLights
नईदुनिया प्रतिनिधि, ग्वालियर। शहर में मौसम का मिजाज धीरे-धीरे बदलने लगा है। पिछले तीन दिनों में रात के तापमान में खास बदलाव नहीं हुआ, लेकिन दिन के तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की गई है। शनिवार को अधिकतम तापमान 32.7 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया था, जो रविवार को 32.3 और सोमवार को घटकर 30 डिग्री सेल्सियस पर आ गया।
इस तरह तीन दिनों में दिन का तापमान 2.7 डिग्री लुढ़क गया। इस तरह सर्द को चुकी सुबह और रात के बाद अब दिन में भी ठंडक आ गई है। सोमवार सुबह हवा में नमी 90 प्रतिशत तक पहुंचने से मौसम में ठंडक का अहसास भी बढ़ा।
रात का तापमान लगभग स्थिर
मौसम विभाग के आंकड़ों के अनुसार, न्यूनतम तापमान शनिवार को 16.3 डिग्री, रविवार को 16.2 डिग्री और सोमवार को 16.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया यानी रात का तापमान लगभग स्थिर बना हुआ है।
इसके विपरीत दिन के तापमान में लगातार गिरावट से सुबह और दोपहर के मौसम में अंतर महसूस किया जा रहा है।
सोमवार को अधिकतम तापमान सामान्य से 0.2 डिग्री कम रहा, जबकि शनिवार को यह सामान्य से 2.5 डिग्री और रविवार को 2.1 डिग्री अधिक था। सुबह 5:30 बजे तापमान 17.4 डिग्री और 8:30 बजे 18 डिग्री दर्ज किया गया।
धीरे-धीरे कम हो रही है दिन की गर्माहट
दोपहर 2:30 बजे तापमान 29.6 डिग्री तक पहुंचा, जबकि शाम 5:30 बजे यह गिरकर 24.2 डिग्री पर आ गया। मौसम में आ रही यह तब्दीली संकेत दे रही है कि दिन की गर्माहट धीरे-धीरे कम हो रही है। हालांकि रात का तापमान अभी 16 डिग्री के आसपास बना हुआ है। ऐसे में सुबह और शाम के समय हल्की ठंडक महसूस होने लगी है।

articles.title: Wind and thunderstorms: all of Île-de-France under a yellow alert this Tuesday - Sortir à Paris
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Arunachal Pradesh
articles.full_text:
Paris and the eight departments of Île-de-France are under a yellow wind and thunderstorm warning this Tuesday, November 17, 2026, according to Météo-France’s 6 a.m. bulletin. Gusts are expected during thunderstorms, and it is a day of strike action: here’s what you need to know.
Paris and the whole of Île-de-France are under a yellow wind and thunderstorm alert this Tuesday, November 17, 2026, just two days after Sunday’s spell of high winds. In its bulletin issued at 6 a.m. on Tuesday, Météo-France has added the risk of thunderstorms to the wind alert for all eight departments in the Île-de-France region: Paris (75), Seine-et-Marne (77), Yvelines (78), Essonne (91), Hauts-de-Seine (92), Seine-Saint-Denis (93), Val-de-Marne (94) and Val-d'Oise (95).
The alert widened further overnight. A total of 73 departments are now under a yellow alert (up from 68 at 4 p.m. Monday), stretching from Brittany to Grand Est via Normandy, Hauts-de-France and Centre. Of these, 46 are affected by thunderstorms, including the whole of Île-de-France. None are under an orange alert at this stage.
The forecaster is nevertheless remaining cautious. On Monday evening, he did not rule out an escalation to orange alert level in western France, Ouest-France reported. The 6 a.m. bulletin did not include it, but the next update is due at 4 p.m. on Tuesday.
Why another burst of wind this Tuesday?
A deepening low-pressure system near the English Channel is crossing the north of the country and significantly strengthening southwesterly winds. The coasts along the English Channel and the Atlantic are most exposed: Meteored is forecasting gusts of 90 to 110 km/h there.
The wind won’t be the only weather to contend with. Showers, sometimes accompanied by thunderstorms, are expected in the afternoon across the northwest and north of the country, and it is precisely during these showers that gusts could be strongest.
Thunderstorms in Paris and the Île-de-France region this Tuesday?
The latest development this Tuesday morning: Météo-France has now placed Paris and its inner and outer suburbs under a yellow thunderstorm warning, in addition to the wind alert. The most active showers are expected in the afternoon, with strong gusts possible beneath storm cells, at times stronger than the day's average wind.
The yellow alert level signals a common but locally dangerous weather phenomenon: not everyone will see a thunderstorm, but where one breaks out, it may bring brief gusts of wind and heavy rain. Advice on how to respond is available on the Météo-France thunderstorm page.
What gusts can be expected in Paris and the Île-de-France region?
In Île-de-France, forecasts call for gusts of 75 to 90 km/h, with gusts potentially reaching nearly 90 km/h in exposed areas of the outer suburbs, according to Planet.
A more severe scenario has been circulating since Monday. Météo-France’s AROME model forecasts gusts of 100 to 110 km/h along a swath stretching from Brittany to Lorraine and passing through southern Île-de-France, from the afternoon into the evening, Météo Paris explains. This remains the less likely scenario, but it puts the peak winds late in the day, just as people are heading home from work.
As for the weather, expect frequent showers and mild temperatures for the time of year, ranging from 12 to 15°C. For a day-by-day breakdown, see our Paris weather forecast for this week.
What precautions should you take when a yellow warning is in effect for wind and thunderstorms?
A yellow weather warning signals usual but locally dangerous conditions, Météo-France reminds us. A few simple precautions are all it takes to get through the day without any nasty surprises:
- put away or secure anything that could be blown off balconies and terraces (plant pots, chairs, parasols);
- avoid stopping or parking under trees because of falling branches;
- put off walks in forests or large parks until a calmer day;
- if cycling or riding a scooter, watch out for crosswinds on bridges and major roads;
- if a storm breaks, take shelter in a solid building, never under a tree;
- unplug sensitive electrical appliances if the storm is approaching.
When the wind picks up, the City of Paris sometimes closes its parks, gardens and cemeteries as a precaution. Before heading out, check paris.fr or your local municipality’s website.
Wind and strikes: how to get around this Tuesday?
The day is shaping up to be a difficult one. Tuesday, November 17, is also a day of strikes and protests in Paris. The march sets off from Place de la Nation at 2 p.m. and heads to Place d’Italie via Boulevard Diderot, Pont d’Austerlitz and Boulevard de l’Hôpital, on a route approved by the police prefecture, according to Ouest-France. If the windiest forecast proves accurate, the gusts will coincide with the end of the march.
For schools, the civil service and calls to strike, we take a look at what to expect in our article on the November 17 strike in Paris. As for trains, the RER D and Line R are expected to be disrupted: for a line-by-line breakdown, see our update on the November 17 SNCF and RATP strike.
Wind can also slow some surface lines, particularly the RER and Transilien, because of branches fallen onto the tracks. Before setting off, it’s best to check our live Metro, RER and train updates.
What to do in Paris this Tuesday despite the wind and thunderstorms?
With gusty winds, thunderstorms and travel disruptions, it’s best to postpone outdoor outings and opt for sheltered spots close to home. Museums, exhibitions and movie theaters make great refuges. Browse our ideas for rainy days or the best things to do in Paris and Île-de-France this week.
Will the wind die down on Wednesday, November 18?
In large part. In its bulletin issued at 6 a.m. on Tuesday, Météo-France no longer has any departments in the Île-de-France region on alert for Wednesday, November 18. Winds will remain strong, however, with gusts of up to 70 km/h, fewer showers and temperatures of 10 to 13°C. In Brittany, Ouest-France even reports unusually prolonged strong winds, lasting until Thursday, November 19.
The run of storms could continue. Météo Paris has not ruled out further gales across the northern half of the country by November 22, though the scenario has yet to be confirmed.
To keep track of developments, the Météo-France weather alert map is updated at least twice a day, at 6 a.m. and 4 p.m. You can also check our Paris weather today and tomorrow every day.

articles.title: IMD Warns of 70 kmph Gusts, Heavy Rainfall Across Odisha on Nov 19-20 - Pragativadi
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Arunachal Pradesh
articles.full_text:
Odisha is on high alert as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued critical forecasts regarding the impact of a potential cyclone heading toward the region.
According to weather officials, the outer band of the developing system is expected to trigger severe weather conditions across the state over the coming days.
Wind and Weather Progression
November 18 (Evening Onward): Surface winds are expected to pick up pace, blowing at 40 to 50 km/h across parts of Odisha.
November 19 to 20 (Night to Afternoon): Sustained wind speeds will increase to 50 to 60 km/h, with powerful squalls and gusty winds reaching up to 70 km/h.
Heavy Rainfall Warnings:
On November 19, heavy downpours are predicted primarily across northern Odisha districts due to the outer band of the system.
Following the landfall on November 20, heavy rainfall is expected to shift and impact southern Odisha districts.
Authorities and local administrations are closely monitoring the situation as citizens in vulnerable areas are advised to stay tuned to official IMD updates and take necessary precautions against high-speed winds and heavy downpours.
